topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture framework on cancer evolution and the tumor microenvironment and outlines the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Mutational Selection and Epigenetic Changes in Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications confer competitive growth advantages that drive micro-scale clonal evolution.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Stem Cell Hierarchy in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how normal tissue hierarchy and stemness characteristics determine which cell populations initiate and propagate cancer.

topics.label: Inflammatory and Microenvironmental Promotion of Tumor Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how external promoters and inflammatory signaling are necessary to induce stem-like states and drive malignant outgrowth in cells carrying dormant mutations.

topics.label: Stromal Dependency of Established Tumors and Therapeutic Targeting
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how established tumors require supportive stromal cells for growth and how targeting this microenvironmental codependency informs cancer therapies.

topics.label: Methodologies for Profiling Tumor Evolution and Spatial Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies used to trace mutational histories and map cell-cell interactions within tumor tissues.

topics.label: Multifactorial Synthesis of Cancer Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates how mutational burden, cell of origin, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental conditions act together to govern cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
